clue.text: Notorious prude is disturbed by statistics chart

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of prude and is are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a chart of statistics is a table of figures

explanation.surface: A notorious prude gets upset when shown a chart of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges PRUDE IS into DISREPU; 'by' just joins it to TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notorious has a bad reputation, which is what being disreputable means.

clue.text: His search is well directed towards a heavenly nature

definitions.meaning: a water dowser hunts for places to sink wells
more godlike, the comparative of an adjective for heavenly

explanation.definitionFit: A dowser seeks underground water for wells; and something more godly is comparatively more heavenly.

clue.text: Seagull dispersed sewage muck

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered about, so the letters of the bird's name are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A seagull scatters the filth from a sewage outfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullage is an old word for refuse, filth or the dirty water from drains.

clue.text: Cockney extremity in the midst of spring feast

indicators.note: in the midst of means placed right inside the other word, splitting it

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival held in spring
an end is an extremity

explanation.surface: A Londoner at the far end of a springtime celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: An EastEnder lives in the East End of London, the traditional home of Cockneys.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, traditionally from the East End.

clue.text: The last formed social class?

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's last is the foot-shaped block on which the top part of a shoe is shaped
as in the ... class, the top rank of society

explanation.definitionFit: The top leather part of a shoe is moulded over a last; the highest social stratum is the upper class.

clue.text: Mien means skylines

parts.note: mien is bearing or manner, as is an air
means or methods are ways

explanation.surface: A person's bearing is a way of getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: Airways are routes through the sky, playfully called skylines.

clue.text: Louisiana rock, but there won't be any more!

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Louisiana
a stone is a piece of rock

explanation.surface: A Louisiana rock sounds like a final example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this is the final one means no more remain.

clue.text: Giving the right illustration regarding spelling

parts.note: ortho- is the Greek-derived prefix meaning straight or correct
a graphic is a picture or illustration

explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthography is the conventional system of spelling, so the adjective concerns spelling.

clue.text: Mutinies, and charges the battery again?

definitions.meaning: read as RE- plus volts, it means puts the voltage back into a cell

explanation.definitionFit: Uprisings are revolts; whimsically, recharging a battery restores its volts.

clue.text: Yearly form of solar protection

parts.note: p.a. abbreviates per annum, Latin for yearly

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaped version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An annual kind of sun protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yearly' looks like a description of the sunshade, but it is the per annum abbreviation; 'form of' signals the rearrangement of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade carried to shield a person from the sun is a kind of protection.

clue.text: Don't touch lease on oil-rig without partners

parts.note: to lease out a property is to let it
an oil well is drilled by a rig
having no companions means being alone

explanation.surface: A lease on a drilling platform with nobody else involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means leave something as it is and avoid meddling.

clue.text: Weed giving egg producer cause for anxiety

parts.note: a hen lays eggs
a bane is a source of persistent trouble or worry

explanation.surface: A weed that worries the farmyard chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbane is a poisonous plant of the nightshade family, a common wild weed.

clue.text: Say the word, and the computer prints it

definitions.meaning: the data displayed or printed by a machine

explanation.definitionFit: To read something out is to voice it; a machine's displayed output is a readout.

clue.text: Eat too much or stick into scrambled egg

indicators.note: stick into means push one piece inside the other
scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of egg are reordered

explanation.surface: Overindulge, or poke a fork into scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a conjunction offering an alternative, but it is a piece of the wordplay; 'scrambled' mixes the egg and 'stick into' pushes the conjunction inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself, overeating greedily.

clue.text: Stage-curtain suggests way to shorten overlong act

definitions.meaning: a theatre curtain lowered between scenes
cutting a scene from a drama makes it shorter

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre curtain dropped between scenes; also a literal instruction to cut a scene.

clue.text: Laughs not if disposed to attack

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of the two words are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Laughing is out of place if one is inclined to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault.

clue.text: Argon develops in electric motors

definitions.note: the definition describes the things by where they are found, the rotating coils inside motors

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for argon
to mature is to develop fully

explanation.surface: The gas argon builds up inside electric motors.
explanation.definitionFit: Armatures are the rotating wound cores found inside dynamos and motors.

clue.text: Screen giant lizard

definitions.meaning: a display screen for a computer or television
a large tropical lizard, as in the Komodo dragon's family

explanation.definitionFit: A display unit; and a large varanid reptile, such as the Nile species.

clue.text: They would hold nine gallons but are almost worthless

definitions.meaning: a pin is a small cask of four and a half gallons, so a pair holds nine
as in not caring two hoots, of very little value

explanation.definitionFit: A pin is an old beer-cask measure of half a firkin; trifles valued at a pair of pins are next to nothing.

clue.text: Deserter with the hump?

parts.note: not a runaway in a sulk but a humped beast that lives in the desert

explanation.definitionFit: The humped ship of the desert is a dweller of sandy wastes.

clue.text: Vessel with poop carrying 101

indicators.note: carrying here means bearing the number at the head, so it comes first

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
the poop is the raised deck at a ship's stern

explanation.surface: A ship with a numbered rear deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank or vessel for holding water.

clue.text: Island similar to hominoid

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is often just Man
like means similar to

explanation.surface: An island resembling an ape-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominoid means resembling a human, which is what being humanlike means.

clue.text: Apparently begging for a press statement

definitions.meaning: with an open palm extended, as a beggar does
a release given to the media

explanation.definitionFit: A beggar holds a palm forward; a printed release distributed to journalists is a handout.

clue.text: Little bird higher than an enormous man

indicators.note: in a down clue, higher than means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird perched above a huge man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so the word means a person of immense size.

clue.text: It supplies artillery backing back streets

indicators.note: backing means going into reverse, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word for streets is read from the end

parts.note: lanes are narrow streets

explanation.surface: A depot sends guns to support the fighting in the backstreets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns RA into AR, and 'back' turns LANES into SENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store from which weapons are issued.

clue.text: Herb is Tom's favourite

definitions.meaning: a tom is a male cat, and this plant drives felines wild

explanation.definitionFit: Nepeta is a scented herb whose smell cats love.

clue.text: Hellenic grandmother with heart turned ice

indicators.note: with heart means given a new middle, so a piece is set inside

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother

indicators.note: turned means twisted round into another order

explanation.surface: A Greek granny whose heart has gone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart' means given a new centre, so the reshuffled ice (signalled by 'turned') replaces nothing and simply sits in the middle of the granny.
explanation.definitionFit: Grecian and Hellenic both mean belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Now taut, formerly taught in grammar classes

parts.note: the present is now
taut means tense, stretched tight

explanation.surface: A contrast of the verb forms of a word, today versus in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now taut, formerly taught' plays on the present and past forms of the verb teach.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form for current time was a staple of old-fashioned grammar lessons.
